newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Former Brazil leader Collor denies Mafia link.
newsitem.headline: Former Brazil leader Collor denies Mafia link.

text.p: Former Brazilian President Fernando Collor, who was toppled amid a corruption scandal in 1992, denied on Tuesday any link to the Italian Mafia and said he was being "absurdly" persecuted by a new probe.

Interviewed by Brazil's Globo television in Miami, where he now lives in self-imposed exile, Collor dismissed reports by police that they had evidence of connections between his murdered former campaign manager and members of the Mafia.

"Why are you asking me if I know these people?" he shouted, thumping a table, when a reporter read out names of Italian criminals that the police said carried out bank transactions with his former aide, Paulo Cesar Farias.
"Why should I have any connection with any form of Mafia? I am an ex-president of the republic, I was judged like nobody else in (Brazil) and cleared by the highest court," Collor said.

Collor was cleared of corruption charges by the Supreme Court in 1994 but remains banned from holding elected office until 2002. Farias was murdered last year after serving 19 months of a seven-year sentence for tax evasion.

Police announced last week a breakthrough in a four-year probe into Farias' business activities after Italian detectives showed them proof of $7.8 million in bank transactions involving accounts of Farias and known Mafia members.
The head of Brazil's federal police said much of the money ended up in bank accounts in Miami, which were being investigated, but declined to say who they belonged to.

In another development in the case which has turned into a real-life Brazilian soap opera, a judge said on Tuesday he had asked a forensic expert to carry out new examinations of evidence collected after Farias' murder in June 1996.

A police investigation found Farias to have been shot in bed by his girlfriend who then committed suicide. But many Brazilians believed he was the victim of assassins. News of the Mafia connection was seized upon as another sign of more sinister forces at work.
In his interview, Collor said he was looking forward to the day when he could again stand for election and clear his name once and for all.
